questions.question: Describe the social structure of early farming societies.
questions.expected_answer: People lived in large families. Families with a common ancestor formed a clan, with a clan name, and people often could not marry within their clan. Elders were respected for their wisdom, ancestors were honoured, and children learnt customs through stories, songs and work.

questions.question: Explain how a chiefdom was governed.
questions.expected_answer: A chief, usually from a royal family, led the chiefdom. He was advised by a council of senior men, and headmen looked after villages. Important matters were discussed at public meetings like the kgotla or imbizo. The chief and council acted as a court. If a chief was unfair, people could leave and join another chief.

questions.question: Describe how people made a living in early farming societies.
questions.expected_answer: Most people farmed crops and kept animals, and cattle were the main wealth. Specialists such as ironworkers and potters made tools and pots. People bartered goods, traded ivory, skins and later gold at the east coast for glass beads and cloth, and gave tribute to the chief, who shared food in hard times.
